A converging lens has f = 20 cm. An object is 30 cm in front. Where is the image formed?
questions.explanation: Lens equation: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/20 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60 → di = 60 cm real image.
steps: Sign shows real image opposite side
questions.fastStrategy: Common combo: 20–30 gives image at 60 cm real and inverted.

questions.question: Wave speed on a string is v = √(T/μ). If tension quadruples while linear density stays the same, speed becomes:
A point light source has intensity I at distance r. At distance 2r, intensity is:
questions.explanation: Inverse-square law: intensity ∝ 1/r^2. Doubling distance makes intensity one-fourth.

questions.question: Unpolarized light passes through an ideal polarizer. What fraction of the original intensity emerges?
questions.explanation: First polarizer transmits the component along its axis, averaging to 50% for unpolarized light.
questions.fastStrategy: One perfect polarizer halves unpolarized light.

questions.question: Two-slit interference: destructive interference at a point means the path difference equals:

choices.D: An integer multiple of λ/4 only

questions.explanation: Destructive interference occurs when path difference is (m + 1/2)λ, i.e., λ/2, 3λ/2, etc.
questions.fastStrategy: Half-odd multiples of λ give canceling waves.

questions.question: A ray inside water (n ≈ 1.33) strikes air at 60° to the normal. What happens?
questions.explanation: Critical angle water→air is θc ≈ arcsin(1/1.33) ≈ 48.8°. At 60° (> θc), total internal reflection occurs.
steps: Conclude TIR when incident exceeds θc
questions.fastStrategy: 60° is well above ~49° critical angle for water, so it totally reflects.
